category_title: Highly anxious or extremely shy students at risk of disengagement
minimal_context: The student is at the playground during lunch break, expected to wait in line and take turns playing 4-square handball with her peers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright, it is time for 4-square handball. Go ahead and line up to wait your turn to get into a square.

STUDENT: (Stands far away from the court, looking down and avoiding the group of nine students waiting in line) ...

TUTOR: You need to join the line with the others.

STUDENT: (Steps further back, refusing to look at the kids her own age) I don't want to go over there.

TUTOR: Just go stand with them and wait.

STUDENT: (Turns her back to the court, completely shutting down and refusing to participate) No. I can't speak to them.

options.A: Use a gentle, not overly directive approach during the lunch break, emphasizing commenting rather than questioning and suggesting rather than instructing.
options.B: Provide the option to participate in 4-square handball with the teacher aide and visiting players, or complete unfinished work inside with supervision.
options.C: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student regarding the 4-square handball game instead of imposing control.
options.D: Reinforce the student on a daily basis with a sticker of her favorite rugby league team for participating in the 4-square handball game.
